change.summary: Fields inside the top-level data object switched from 'omitted when absent' to 'present with JSON null' — serviceTrigger, averageEnergyConsumption, batteryChargeLevel and others, sitting alongside normal {timestamp, unit, value} objects. HTTP stayed 200 and every other value was correct. Clients mapping data values into a typed model crashed.

changelog.note: developer.volvocars.com is Akamai-blocked to automated fetches, so a quietly-added portal note cannot be fully ruled out. What is verified is that none of roughly fifteen affected developers — including the integration's code owner, who learned of it from user reports — referenced one.

contract.note: Detectable ONLY with per-field type tracking. The status stayed 200 and no key name changed; a monitor diffing status codes or key sets alone misses it completely. You have to record that data.serviceTrigger was an object and is now null. Also account-gated: it needs a real VIN and OAuth token, so it is not publicly probeable.

notes: Two physically independent Home Assistant instances — different houses, networks, ISPs, credentials and car models — went from good values to unavailable 81 seconds apart, which is about as clean a server-side attribution as field evidence gets. The client library had gone ten months between releases, so nothing changed on the caller side. This is the case that proves response-shape checking must be typed rather than presence-based.
